extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism claims from SEM, qPCR, and homology-model sections/figures, replacing automated locator notes with bounded evidence classes.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SibaDef-treated S. aureus and B. subtilis cells showed SEM-visible membrane/cell-envelope disruption at 1x MIC; this supports a direct cell-envelope disruption mechanism for the tested Gram-positive bacteria.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: SibaDef against Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 6538 and Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633
mechanism_claims.limitations: SEM morphology supports membrane/cell-envelope disruption context; it is not a quantitative permeabilization kinetics assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SibaDef expression in whole black fly bodies increased after oral feeding with S. aureus or B. subtilis, peaking at 36 h in the reported time course.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: SibaDef transcript response in Simulium bannaense after bacterial feeding

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=27:Transcription of SibaDef in black flies fed on bacteria;xml:fig=6:Figure 6

mechanism_claims.limitations: Expression induction is host response context and should not be promoted to a direct antimicrobial killing mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Homology modeling places SibaDef in an insect defensin-like fold with alpha/beta structural elements and surface basic residues; this is structural context, not experimental target validation.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Computational homology modeling and charge mapping do not prove a direct molecular target.
